children: By Emese Bartha and Patrick Sheridan
U.S. Treasury yields moved higher as oil prices erased early declines, though long-dated yields still remain comfortably below recent multidecade highs.
The 10-year Treasury yield rose 5 basis points, to 5.148%, according to Tradeweb.

Investors are also looking ahead to next week's Fed meeting with the CME's FedWatch tool indicating only about a 17% chance of a rate rise. Around three rate increases are priced in over the coming 12 months.

BMO rate strategists expect a hold. "In the wake of last week's CPI/PPI/Import Prices, the Fed's favored measure of consumer price pressures is effectively priced into the market," they say in a note.
RBC BlueBay Asset Management expects U.S. inflation to peak at 4% early in the new year, fixed income CIO Mark Dowding said in a note.
Barclays also upgraded its forecast and now expects the Fed to boost by a quarter point in December and January, having previously expected just one increase in December.
Yields on French government bonds rose on concerns about violent street demonstrations in France in the wake of the government's planned budget-deficit cut.

The protests heightened concerns about political uncertainty ahead of next year's presidential elections, on top of worries about debt. French bonds considerably underperformed U.S. and European peers.

The 10-year French OAT yield increased 14.1 basis points, to 4.925%, while 10-year German Bund yields increased 4.2 basis points, to 3.453%. The spread between the two is 147.3 basis points, LSEG data showed, with Monday's intraday high 148.3 bps, the highest since Oct. 5.
Violence in France escalated during a nationwide protest on Saturday, then resumed Sunday evening with riots across Paris.

"What started as student/education unease about a month ago morphed into broad protest against the rising cost of living, declining public services and overall frustration against the Macron administration," KBC Bank analysts said in a note.
French politicians have to bridge the domestic riots with international bond-market pressure while trying to navigate next year's budget through parliament, they said.

With French public debt above 119% of gross domestic product and the deficit expected to remain substantially above the European Union's 3% threshold, investors are increasingly questioning the government's ability to stabilize public finances, Claudio Wewel, FX strategist at J. Safra Sarasin Sustainable Asset Management, said in a note.
